source_refs.note: Topic 19.8 with the classification by size and the For Information box on mutagens (PDF 142-143).

blocks.text: A mutation is a change in the content of the genetic message. Mutations range from small, such as a change in one or a few nucleotides, to large, such as a change in a large segment of a chromosome or a whole chromosome.

items: Point mutations: change only one or a few nucleotides.
Chromosomal mutations: large-scale changes in the position of genes or in the structure or number of chromosomes.

blocks.title: For information
blocks.text: Agents that cause mutations are mutagens, and the organism or cell in which a mutation occurs is a mutant.

blocks.prompt: What is the difference between a mutagen and a mutant?
blocks.explanation: A mutagen causes mutations; a mutant is the organism or cell that carries the mutation.

items: Mutation: change in the genetic message, from one nucleotide to whole chromosomes.
Two types by size: point and chromosomal.
